OpenAI’s @thsottiaux explains how dots work and how OpenAI has been deploying specialist dots internally:

“The agent never stops. Occasionally it sleeps. But it’s always online, always doing proactive research, thinking about your goals, thinking about your preferences.”

“You just give your dot a little bit of feedback. It learns.”

“A couple days in, you’re like, ‘Wow, I can’t really quite imagine doing work without this thing.’”

“You don’t have to be super technical but just kind of still feel the power of it.”

Inside OpenAI, specialist dots are already being provisioned with their own identities, permissions, machines, and roles:

“We have them running on Mac minis.”

“We provision them exactly like employees. We mint a new little identity, and then it’s got this IAM and the roles.”

“We give them a very premium machine as well because the model is incredibly capable under the hood.”

“So your dot can just use a computer just like you would.”

“We have these set up inside of OpenAI. They do all sorts of things, including procurement, for example.”

candidates.text:
If your email open rate is below 25%, you’ll be burning money in Q4

You don't need a "better subject line." You need a better deliverability and segmentation strategy

Here is how you fix a dead list in 3 steps:

1. Mass Suppress the Dead Weight. Gmail and Outlook see you blasting people who haven't opened in months and immediately flag you as spam. Stop sending. Create a strict 90-day unengaged segment and suppress them. Yes, all of them

2. Run a Sunsetting Sequence. Before they are permanently gone, send a 2-step plain-text re-engagement offer (e.g., “Are you still interested?” + “Final check-in before suppression”). If they click, they re-enter the main list. If they ignore, they are permanently suppressed

3. Hyper-Segment your Sending. Instead of blasting your full list 3x a week, change your strategy. Start sending 2x a week to only your 60-day or 30-day "active openers." Build up trust with the inbox providers. When your domain reputation is restored, then you can slowly expand the active window back out

Fix the fundamentals, and your open rates will recover

Blasting a dead list is not a strategy
